title: Supported perfect restriction data on a compact-open overlap model
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], $W$ a compact open and $V$ an affine open, and let $T\subseteq X$ be closed with compact complement. Choose derived localizations [def-pc-derived-category] with common Hom universe $w$ on $W,V$, their localized open sites, and $W\cap V$. Let $F\in D(\mathcal O_W)$ be perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] with every cohomology stalk vanishing outside $T$. Write $S_W,S_V$ for transported overlap restriction [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. There exist a compact open $U\subseteq V$, chosen derived localizations on $U$ and every localized open site of $U$ in universe $w$, and a perfect $G\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ such that the inverse image $T_V$ of $T$ in $V$ is closed with compact complement and every cohomology stalk of $G$ vanishes outside the inverse image of $T_V$. There is an equivalence $e:D(\mathcal O_U)\simeq D(\mathcal O_{W\cap V})$, a natural isomorphism $J_U\mathbin{\ggg}e\cong S_V$, and an isomorphism $e(G\oplus G[1])\cong S_W(F\oplus F[1])$. No object on all of $V$ and no morphism lifting is asserted.

source.place: Overlap restriction input to the supported affine extension step using Tag 08EK

proof.text: Set U = V.ι inverse-image W. The image of U under subtype inclusion is V intersect W. Apply IsCompact.inter_of_isOpen in the quasi-separated ambient scheme, using hV.isCompact and hW, and transfer compactness back through IsEmbedding.subtypeVal.isCompact_iff. Closedness of the inverse image of T follows from continuity; its complement has image V intersect the open compact complement of T. The same intersection lemma proves compactness of this complement.

Transport the given localization on the localized site of V at U across Modules.overEquiv U to obtain hD. The private helper hasDerivedCategory_of_equivalence constructs the localization by composing the termwise equivalence with DerivedCategory.Q and verifies its universal property through Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalence_source. Obtain the family hO using nonempty_derivedOpenLocalization U.toScheme. Define j = V.ι restricted to W, R = Modules.restrictFunctor j, and G = R.mapDerivedCategory.obj F. No object is chosen from an unproved existence assertion.

Identify exact R with Modules.tensorPullback j by uniqueness of left adjoints. The localization-derived functor of this exact tensor pullback and derivedPullback j are isomorphic by leftDerivedUnique, using exists_derivedPullback. Apply derivedPullback_preserve_perfect and transport each local strictly perfect witness along this isomorphism. For support, mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso and Modules.restrictStalkNatIso identify each homology stalk of G at x with that of F at j(x). The equation morphismRestrict_base_coe identifies their ambient points; injectivity of the stalk isomorphism transfers Subsingleton.

Construct s : U.toScheme ≅ (W inf V).toScheme as V.ι.isoImage U followed by X.isoOfEq (V.functor_map_eq_inf W). Pushforward along s and its inverse gives the exact module equivalence E and hence e = E.mapDerivedCategory. By uniqueness of left adjoints E.functor is restriction along s.inv. Composing with U.ι or j gives respectively the two ambient overlap inclusions, verified by cancel_mono on V.ι and W.ι. Modules.overFunctorEquiv, overMapCompOverEquiv and restrictFunctorComp give the underived restriction squares; mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso descend both to derived natural isomorphisms. The V square supplies the first requested comparison. The W square, together with R.mapDerivedCategory.mapBiprod and commShiftIso, supplies the final comparison on F plus F[1]. All constructions include empty opens and empty support.

proof_origin.based_on: Original Stacks 09IM overlap restriction plan; existing exact-derived functor comparisons and the proved derived-pullback preservation theorem (09UA).

mathlib_searches.query: Restriction to an open subscheme preserves locally perfect complexes and vanishing homology stalks; affine supported extension plus shift
A perfect complex restricts to a perfect complex on an open subscheme; the direct sum with its shift has the same closed support.
